translation_en: Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: Ibn Wahb narrated to us. Harmalah ibn Yahya al-Tujibi narrated to me—these are his words: Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus ibn Yazid informed me, from Ibn Shihab: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf informed me that Aishah said: When the Messenger of Allah was commanded to give his wives a choice, he began with me and said, “I am going to tell you something, but do not be hasty; consult your parents first.” She said: He knew that my parents would never tell me to leave him. Then he said, “Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said, ‘O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you in a gracious manner. But if you desire Allah, His Messenger, and the Home of the Hereafter, then Allah has prepared a great reward for those of you who do good’” Quran 33:28. She said: I replied, “About what would I consult my parents? I desire Allah, His Messenger, and the Home of the Hereafter.” She said: The other wives of the Messenger of Allah did as I had done.

Surayj ibn Yunus narrated to us: Abbad ibn Abbad narrated to us, from Asim, from Muadhah al-Adawiyyah, from Aishah, who said: After the verse was revealed, “You may defer whomever of them you will and receive to yourself whomever you will” Quran 33:51, the Messenger of Allah would ask our permission when it was another wife’s day. Muadhah asked her, “What would you say to the Messenger of Allah when he asked your permission?” She said, “If the choice were mine, I would not prefer anyone over myself.”
Al-Hasan ibn Isa narrated this to us: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us: Asim informed us, with this chain and a similar report.

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi informed us: Abthar informed us, from Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Sha‘bi, from Masruq, who said: Aishah said, “The Messenger of Allah gave us a choice, but we did not count it as a divorce.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated this to us: Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Sha‘bi, from Masruq, who said: “I would not care whether I gave my wife a choice once, a hundred times, or a thousand times, as long as she chose me. I asked Aishah, and she said, ‘The Messenger of Allah gave us a choice. Was that a divorce?’”

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Asim, from al-Sha‘bi, from Masruq, from Aishah, that the Messenger of Allah gave his wives a choice, and it was not a divorce.

Ishaq ibn Mansur informed me: Abd al-Rahman informed us, from Sufyan, from Asim al-Ahwal and Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Sha‘bi, from Masruq, from Aishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah gave us a choice, and we chose him; he did not count it as a divorce.

Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, and Abu Kurayb narrated to us. Yahya said: Abu Muawiyah informed us. The other two said: Abu Muawiyah narrated to us, from al-A‘mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, from Aishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah gave us a choice, and we chose him; he did not count it as anything against us.

Abu al-Rabi al-Zahrani narrated to me: Ismail ibn Zakariyya narrated to us: al-A‘mash narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from Aishah; and from al-A‘mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, from Aishah, with a similar report.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Rawh ibn Ubadah narrated to us: Zakariyya ibn Ishaq narrated to us: Abu al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: Abu Bakr asked permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah and found people sitting at his door; none of them had been admitted. Abu Bakr was given permission and entered. Then Umar came and asked permission; he was admitted and found the Prophet sitting, with his wives around him, silent and distressed. Umar said, “I will say something to make the Prophet laugh.” He said, “Messenger of Allah, if you had seen the daughter of Kharijah asking me for maintenance, I stood up and struck her neck.” The Messenger of Allah laughed and said, “These women around me, as you see, are asking me for maintenance.” Abu Bakr stood and went to Aishah, striking her neck; Umar stood and went to Hafsah, striking her neck. Each said, “You are asking the Messenger of Allah for what he does not have.” They said, “By Allah, we will never ask the Messenger of Allah for anything he does not have.” Then he stayed apart from them for a month, or twenty-nine days. Then this verse was revealed to him: “O Prophet, say to your wives…” until “a great reward for those of you who do good” Quran 33:28–29. He began with Aishah and said, “Aishah, I want to present something to you. I would like you not to be hasty about it until you consult your parents.” She said, “What is it, Messenger of Allah?” He recited the verse to her. She said, “Should I consult my parents about you, Messenger of Allah? Rather, I choose Allah, His Messenger, and the Home of the Hereafter. I ask you not to tell any of your wives what I have said.” He said, “No woman among them will ask me without my telling her. Allah did not send me to make things difficult or to seek difficulty; He sent me as a teacher who makes things easy.”
